newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC plans extra 200 mln stg spending in U.K. plant.
newsitem.headline: NEC plans extra 200 mln stg spending in U.K. plant.

text.p: Japan's leading semiconductor manufacturer NEC Corp announced on Thursday that it plans to make an additional investment of 200 million pounds in its chip plant in Livingston, Scotland.
The investment would add another 200 jobs to the 560 at the second factory in Livingston, which started mass production in October 1996, the company said in a statement.

NEC said that the spending will take Wafer Fabrication Plant Number Two to 0.25 micron technology by March 1998 and will considerably increase production capacity from 20,000 wafers per month to 30,000 in the second half of fiscal 1998.
NEC invested 530 million pounds for the second plant to produce 20,000 wafers per month using 0.35 micron process technology, which enables production of top of the line 64-megabit DRAM chips.
NEC plans to be producing one and a half million of the memory devices per month by the time the 0.25 micron technology is introduced in March 1998.
